title: Registration of Births and Deaths Bill
what_it_is: Registration of Births and Deaths Bill

sections.label: Birth death stillbirth reporting changes
sections.summary: The Bill aims to streamline birth, death and stillbirth reporting and registration, introducing six key changes to the RBDA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The main objective is to streamline the birth, death and stillbirth reporting and registration processes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Bill will introduce six key changes to the RBDA.

sections.label: Penalty for failure to report
sections.summary: Failure to report without reasonable excuse carries a fine up to $1,500, imprisonment up to one month, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Failure to report, without a reasonable excuse, will result in a fine not exceeding $1,500 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding one month, or both.

sections.label: Delayed registration concept removed
sections.summary: The concept of delayed registration is no longer relevant and will be removed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The concept of a delayed registration is no longer relevant in today's context and will be removed.

sections.label: Second step removed
sections.summary: Under the Bill, the second step will be removed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, the second step will be removed.

sections.label: Automatic death registration and certificate
sections.summary: The RG automatically registers the death under clause 24, after which a relative may download the digital death certificate from My Legacy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The death will then be automatically registered by the RG under clause 24.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Once the death is registered by the RG, the deceased person’s relative may download the digital death certificate from the My Legacy website, a one-stop portal for post-death matters.

sections.label: Registration before Coroner certificate
sections.summary: Under clause 25, the RG may register a death before a Coroner's certificate is issued if satisfied of the death in Singapore and the deceased's identity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Under clause 25 of the Bill, the RG may register such a death before a Coroner’s certificate is issued, if the RG is satisfied from the information and evidence provided as to the occurrence of the death in Singapore and the identity of the deceased person.

sections.label: Bill offences and raised penalties
sections.summary: The Bill prescribes offences in clauses 48 to 53 and raises penalties across the board, which have not been raised since 1937.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Bill also prescribes offences in clauses 48 to 53 in relation to: (a) the provision of false or misleading statement or information; (b) the unauthorised access to or interference with the registers; (c) the forging of or tampering with certificates or extracts; (d) the obstruction of the performance of functions or exercise of powers by the RG or an authorised registration officer; and (e) offences by corporations and unincorporated associations or partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In addition, the penalties under the Bill will be raised across the board to ensure deterrence, given that the penalties in the current Act have not been raised since 1937.

sections.label: Hospital deaths registered automatically
sections.summary: A medical practitioner certifies the cause of death online, and the RG automatically registers the death, so relatives need not do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: When a person passes away in a hospital, a medical practitioner will examine the body and certify the cause of death online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: These death particulars are conveyed electronically to the RG, who will automatically register the death; the relatives no longer need to do this.

sections.label: Digital death certificate download
sections.summary: The RG automatically registers the death upon receiving death particulars electronically, and the relative may download the digital death certificate from My Legacy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Second Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The RG will automatically register the death upon receiving the death particulars electronically from the medical practitioner, and the relative may then download the digital death certificate from the My Legacy website.

sections.label: Birth registration on incomplete particulars
sections.summary: Under new section 9(2), the Registrar-General may register a child's birth based on incomplete particulars if the birth is capable of being registered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the new section 9(2), the Registrar-General may register a child’s birth based on incomplete particulars if the birth is capable of being registered on the basis of the incomplete particulars.

sections.label: Stateless people in Singapore
sections.summary: Minister Shanmugam shared that as of 30 November 2020, there were 1,109 stateless people living in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Minister Shanmugam shared in February this year that as of 30 November 2020, there were 1,109 stateless people living in Singapore.

sections.label: Support for unwed mothers
sections.summary: MSF shared median incomes of single unwed parents below 35, and the question asks whether ICA informs MSF of births without a married father.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In November 2018, MSF shared that the median incomes of single unwed parents below 35 years old was in the range of $500 to $700 from the years of 2013 to 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share whether ICA informs MSF when a birth is registered without a father or with a father who is not married to the mother, so that appropriate support, where needed, can be offered to these mothers right from the start?

sections.label: Mixed parentage race classification
sections.summary: Rising inter-ethnic marriages make it important for children of such unions to grow up appreciating their mixed parentage if parents choose double-barrelled race classifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With inter-ethnic marriages going up from 18.4% of all marriages in 2009 to 22.9% in 2019, it is important for children of such unions to have the opportunity to grow up with an appreciation of their mixed parentage, if their parents choose to signify that by choosing double-barrelled race classifications for their children.

sections.label: Double-barrelled race option uptake
sections.summary: In the first two months of 2011, parents of one in five newborn babies of mixed parentage chose the double-barrelled race option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Amongst them, what is the proportion of children who have been assigned double-barrelled race by their parents?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I note that in the first two months of 2011, the parents of one in five newborn babies of mixed parentage chose the double-barrelled race option based on data that the Government released back then.

sections.label: Possible funeral arrangement delays
sections.summary: The Bill may inadvertently delay funeral arrangements if medical practitioners are delayed in electronically registering a death, despite the 24-hour reporting restriction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would the Bill possibly inadvertently bring about delays in the funeral arrangements in some cases, especially if the death occurs at home and the medical practitioner would need to return to his or her office to register the death electronically – and he or she could possibly be delayed in performing that action by the need to attend to other medical cases, for example?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There is a 24-hour time restriction for medical practitioners to report a death but when making funeral arrangements, a matter of hours can cause inconvenience and emotional distress.

sections.label: Funeral directors and deceased NRICs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether relatives can enlist funeral directors to access digital death certificates and whether providers must destroy deceased persons' physical NRICs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Alternatively, will the relatives be able to enlist the help of a funeral director, for example, to access the digital death certificate on their behalf if they give their consent?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Based from feedback from the funeral service industry, funeral directors often come to possess the NRIC of the deceased person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some funeral service providers may accumulate many such NRICs over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This creates the potential for criminal use to be made of these cards if they fall into the wrong hands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In view of this, will the Government consider requiring all funeral service providers and any unrelated persons in possession of physical NRICs of deceased persons to destroy those cards?

sections.label: Reporting duties and overseas deaths
sections.summary: The passage questions the reporting duty on unrelated persons under clause 22(2)(d), whether a jogger finding a body must report, and registration of deaths occurring overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, the Bill also requires in some cases under clause 22(2)(d) the duty for reporting of a death to fall on persons that may not be at all related or associated to the deceased, therefore, there is this undue burden, failing which the person will be considered guilty of an offence and fined up to $1,500 and/or imprisonment of up to a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Minister of State had earlier mentioned about unnatural death briefly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, for the clarity of the public, can the Minister of State clarify if, for example, a person on a morning jog finds a dead body and calls the Police, would the person still be liable to report the death to a medical practitioner under this section?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will alerting the death to the authorities suffice to discharge such a person from the duties the Bill now appears to place on that person?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And four, I have come across a resident whose parents passed away overseas and have not been able to get the death certificate even after he claimed the relevant agencies had assisted him to contact their counterparts in the foreign country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister of State clarify if the process to prevent fraud for such cases has been streamlined and if the Registrar-General will have the discretion to register a death that has occurred outside Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill will not only streamline the process and help the registration of births and deaths through the use of digital platforms but, more importantly, it will also help reduce the possibility of errors and quicken the administrative process for registration of deaths within which grieving families have to go through to lay their loved ones to rest.

sections.label: Mosque funeral arrangements
sections.summary: COVID-19 restrictions and smaller flats make home funeral arrangements difficult, so mosques help make between eight and 10 funeral arrangements daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is, perhaps, due to COVID-19 restrictions and also because new flats are less sizeable and have space limitations, making it difficult for the deceased person’s family to make funeral arrangements and perform funeral prayers in their own home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Therefore, mosques have been helping to make between eight and 10 funeral arrangements daily.

sections.label: Discharge of responsible persons
sections.summary: Section 22(4) discharges every other responsible person's responsibility when just one responsible person complies, even if another had an earlier chance to report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Thirdly, in cases where there is more than one responsible person, section 22(4) discharges responsibility of every other responsible persons by the compliance of just one responsible person, even if there was an earlier opportunity to report by that other person.

sections.label: Mandatory reporting of births
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes amendments making it mandatory for all births to be reported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On the registration of births, I welcome the amendments to make it mandatory for all births to be reported.

sections.label: Department for investigations
sections.summary: The passage asks which department such investigations would fall under if not otherwise covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If not, under which department would such investigations fall under?

sections.label: Time saved from death registrations
sections.summary: About 18,000 hours per year can be saved by the public and Government agencies from not performing over-the-counter death registrations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: This will also save time for members of the public and the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We estimate that a total of about 18,000 hours per year can be saved by members of the public and the relevant Government agencies from not having to perform over-the-counter death registrations.

sections.label: No extra death registration fees
sections.summary: Public hospitals have committed to not charging extra fees for death registration under the streamlined process.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The public hospitals have also committed to not charging extra fees for death registration under the streamlined process.

sections.label: Digitalisation of certificates
sections.summary: Digitalisation starts with birth, death and stillbirth certificates issued under the new Act, with digital extracts for earlier registrations in a later phase.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: To clarify, the digitalisation of documents will start with birth, death and stillbirth certificates that will be issued when the new Act comes into force.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The issuance of digital extracts for births, deaths and stillbirths that are registered before the new Act comes into force will be introduced in a later phase.

sections.label: Missing persons reports average
sections.summary: The Police received an average of about 1,700 missing persons reports per year over the past five years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In the past five years, the Police received an average of about 1,700 missing persons reports per year.

sections.label: Births not registered in 2020
sections.summary: In 2020, 72 births were not registered within 42 days.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In 2020, 72 births were not registered within 42 days.

sections.label: Births to foreigner parents
sections.summary: In the past three years, about 17% of total births were to two foreigner parents, and in 2020 such births were under 0.15%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In the past three years, about 17% of total births in Singapore are those of children born to parents who are both foreigners and, therefore, do not qualify for Singapore Citizenship by birth.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In 2020, such births make up less than 0.15% of total births in Singapore.

sections.label: Double-barrelled race registration
sections.summary: Parents may register a double-barrelled race if they have different registered races, without needing to be across CMIO categories.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For double-barrelled race, parents are allowed to register as long as they have different registered races; they do not need to be across the CMIO categories.

sections.label: NRIC abuse penalties
sections.summary: Under the National Registration Act, anyone abusing NRICs is liable for a fine up to $10,000 or imprisonment up to 10 years or both.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Under the National Registration Act, anyone abusing NRICs is liable for a fine up to $10,000 or imprisonment of up to 10 years or both.

sections.label: ICA officers as registration officers
sections.summary: ICA Enforcement Division investigation officers will be appointed as authorised registration officers to search and investigate suspected offences under part 8 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Investigation officers from ICA's existing Enforcement Division, which currently already investigates offences under Acts such as the Passports Act and National Registration Act, will be appointed as authorised registration officers to conduct searches and investigations into suspected offences under part 8 of the Bill.

sections.label: Public hospitals death registration fees
sections.summary: Public hospitals committed to not charging extra fees for death registration under the streamlined process.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The public hospitals have also committed to not charging extra fees for death registration under the streamlined process.
